answer.rationale: Competitive pricing pressure on SMB creates urgency, but exp_73 definitively shows that targeted discounting acquires poor-quality cohorts with -12% retention. This would worsen churn, not solve it. Instead, referral_incentive (memory_57) adds qualified revenue from established customers—those with proven retention and willingness to advocate. This addresses the immediate churn conversation by offering existing customers tangible value while recruiting new accounts through trusted channels, which historically carry better retention than discount-driven acquisition. Referral incentives preserve margin, reward loyalty, and sidestep the retention cliff documented in memory_73. A standard experiment tests effectiveness in the current competitive moment without broad rollout risk. This approach is grounded in durable memory but does not over-generalize; uncertainty about effectiveness in this specific competitive scenario is preserved.
